Generate a round report

Source: R/report.R
delphi_report.Rd

Writes a self-contained report of a Delphi study, in HTML or Word format, ready to be shared with the research team or attached to the controlled feedback of the next round. The report contains:

  • an overview of the study and, optionally, the list of item statements;

  • a methods section stating the consensus and stability criteria, with references;

  • panel participation and retention across rounds;

  • for each indicator, summary statistics, consensus and item status at the assessed round, stability between consecutive rounds, and the distribution and trend figures;

  • the consensus heat map and, with two or more indicators, the two-indicator map;

  • the items to be submitted to a further round.

Usage

delphi_report(
  x,
  file,
  title = "Delphi study: round report",
  author = NULL,
  round = NULL,
  item_labels = NULL,
  threshold = 0.2,
  relative_to = c("points", "range"),
  method = c("wilcoxon", "scheibe", "both"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  scheibe = 0.15,
  type = 7,
  paired = NULL,
  open = interactive(),
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A delphi_data object.

file

Path of the report. The extension sets the format: .html for HTML, .docx for Microsoft Word.

title, author

Title and author(s) shown in the report header. author may be NULL.

round

Round to assess, for each indicator. NULL (default) uses the last round; see delphi_status().

item_labels

Optional named character vector with the full statement of each item, named by item code, for example c(E1 = "Remote work becomes the norm", E2 = "..."). By default, the labels stored in x (see delphi_data() and read_delphi()) are used.

threshold, relative_to

Consensus rule, see delphi_consensus().

method, alpha, scheibe, paired

Stability rule, see delphi_stability().

type

Quantile algorithm; see delphi_describe().

open

Whether to open the report once it has been created.

quiet

Whether to suppress the rendering messages.

Value

The path of the report, invisibly.

Details

The report requires the rmarkdown and knitr packages and a Pandoc installation; Pandoc is included in RStudio. All text is in English.

Examples

x <- delphi_data(delphi_example, expert_col = "expert",
                 round_col = "round", indicator_col = "indicator",
                 scale = list(impact = c(1, 10), plausibility = c(1, 100)))
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE) &&
    rmarkdown::pandoc_available()) {
  out <- delphi_report(x, file.path(tempdir(), "report.html"), open = FALSE)
  file.exists(out)
}
#> [1] TRUE
# }
